definition: Whisper is a machine learning model for speech recognition and transcription, created by OpenAI and first released as open-source software in September 2022.
details: It is capable of transcribing speech in English and multiple other languages, and can translate several non-English languages into English. Whisper is a weakly-supervised deep learning acoustic model, made using an encoder-decoder transformer architecture. OpenAI claims that the combination of different training data and post-training filtering used in its development has led to improved recognition of accents, background noise, and jargon compared to previous approaches. While the model does not outperform larger, more specialized models and still experiences AI hallucination, it has been shown to be useful for general sound recognition and has many applications across different industries.

explainer.lead: Whisper is an open-source speech recognition and transcription model released by OpenAI in September 2022. It matters because it transcribes many languages, translates non-English speech into English, and was trained to handle accents, background noise and jargon better than earlier approaches.

tiers.eli5: It listens to audio and writes down what was said, in many languages, and can even turn other languages into English text.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run it for transcription and translation pipelines; it is a weakly-supervised encoder-decoder transformer trained on filtered data. A pitfall is hallucination: it can produce text that was not spoken, and it does not beat larger, more specialized models.
tiers.paperLevel: A weakly-supervised deep learning acoustic model using an encoder-decoder transformer architecture, trained on diverse data with post-training filtering. Known limits: it does not outperform larger specialized models and still experiences AI hallucination.

explainer.example: Feed it a noisy recording of accented speech and it returns a transcript, or translates the non-English speech into English text.
